output.summary: The diff changes the upper-bound check from `index < length` to `index <= length`, which violates the documented contract that valid indices are 0 through length-1 and that empty collections have no valid index. This is a high-confidence correctness/regression defect.

findings.title: Off-by-one: `index === length` is incorrectly reported as in-bounds
findings.body: The contract states that for nonnegative integer length the valid integer indices are 0 through length-1, and empty collections have no valid index. Changing the comparison from `< length` to `<= length` makes `inBounds(length, length)` return true and makes `inBounds(0, 0)` return true for an empty collection, both of which are out of bounds. This breaks the public function contract that the change was intended to preserve.
findings.evidence: Current source reads `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. The diff changed `index < length` to `index <= length`. For length=0, index=0 now returns true even though an empty collection has no valid index; for length=N, index=N now returns true even though the maximum valid index is N-1.
findings.suggestion: Restore the strict comparison: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`
